public.prompt: A custom star-rating is already registered through `NG_VALUE_ACCESSOR`. Clicks call the registered change callback, blur calls the touch callback, and `setDisabledState` updates the buttons. Only `formControl.setValue(4)` fails to repaint because `writeValue` currently calls the change callback instead of updating the displayed stars. Which correction restores the intended direction?

options.label: Subscribe to the parent control's `valueChanges` inside the rating and repaint from that separate stream.
Update the displayed stars inside `writeValue`, and invoke the change callback only for user clicks.
Replace the accessor with `@Input() value` and `@Output() valueChange`, then let each parent repaint it.

answerProof.summary: A ControlValueAccessor keeps model-to-view writes separate from view-to-model notifications: `writeValue` renders the incoming model value, while the registered change callback is reserved for user-originated changes.
decisiveConstraints: Programmatic model writes must update the component view without being reported back as fresh user input.
The already-correct click, blur, and disabled channels must keep their existing ownership.

claims.statement: `ControlValueAccessor.writeValue` receives programmatic model-to-view writes, while the registered change callback propagates view changes back to Angular forms.

optionRationales.explanation: Reaching into a parent control creates a second synchronization path and couples the reusable widget to one host instead of honoring the accessor callback it already receives.
optionRationales.plausibility: A valueChanges subscription would observe programmatic updates from that particular control.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: Model-to-view updates must travel through the existing accessor contract for any compatible forms directive.

optionRationales.explanation: `writeValue` owns rendering an incoming model value; only a user click should invoke the registered view-to-model change callback.
A general input/output pair abandons the forms integration that already supplies touch, disabled, and model-write channels.
optionRationales.plausibility: An input and output can support manual two-way synchronization in a parent component.
optionRationales.falsifyingConstraint: The rating must continue participating in Angular forms without per-parent glue code.
